videos.title: Claude vs Grafsy: Which AI Should an Editing Agency Use?
videos.h1: Claude vs Grafsy: Which AI Should an Editing Agency Use?
videos.desc: I timed Claude and Grafsy adding graphics to the same talking head video: 25 minutes vs 12:46. What each one does, where it falls short, and how to choose.
videos.summary: To add graphics to a finished talking head video, Grafsy took 12 minutes 46 seconds with no work from me. Claude took about 25 minutes but did the whole edit, cuts included, and flagged problems in my script. Which one to use depends on the job.
takeaways: Why graphics are the slow part of a talking head video.
What Claude did with one sentence: cut, graphics and a self-check in about 25 minutes.
What Grafsy does with a finished video, and the 12:46 clock time.
The honest limits: no font control in Grafsy, a finished file only from Claude.
How to choose, and what to tell a client before you promise anything.
body: I used one video: me talking to a camera for 18 minutes and 14 seconds about making micro products in under 48 hours. No graphics, no chapters, just a face. I ran the same clock on both ways of fixing it and never paused the timer.
Way 1: hand the whole video to Claude

I gave Claude one sentence, edit this video for YouTube, and told it what the video was about. With no editing software on my computer, it cut and built the video with ffmpeg, a free command-line tool. It transcribed the audio, pulled sample frames, rendered the edit and listened to its own cut to check it had not chopped any words in half.

It also flagged problems I never asked about. I said almost 40 people bought in one place and almost 30 in another, and fixing that means re-recording a line. It put a sales-total card where my script needed a screenshot I did not have. It noted there was no music and the end card did not point to a next video. The whole job took about 25 minutes.
Way 2: Grafsy adds graphics to a finished video

Grafsy does one job. You upload a finished video, it listens to what you say, makes graphics out of your words, and you download the new version. No prompt and no timeline. Upload took about 100 seconds, then it worked in the background. The app reported an 11 minute 6 second render, and the full clock time was 12 minutes 46 seconds.
This is not a fair fight

Claude had a bigger job: cuts, graphics and a review. Grafsy only added graphics to a video that was already finished. So the clock does not say Grafsy is better. It says Grafsy is faster at one job. If that job is most of what you do, that is your hours back every week.

I earn a share of the profit when someone buys Grafsy, so here is where it falls short. It has no precise controls for fonts, and its own page says it helps but does not guarantee results. It is built for English first. If a client has brand fonts or wants one graphic gone, you cannot fix it by hand inside Grafsy today. Claude gives you a finished video file, not a project you can open and adjust, and it took longer. But it asked before swapping in the screenshot and told me what was wrong without being asked.

In the video, Grafsy plans started at $79, one-time rather than a subscription, billed by the second with one credit equal to one minute of video. Commercial and client use is included, and lifetime means the platform stays available, not unlimited videos. Prices change, so check the Grafsy page on the day you watch.
Finished talking video and you only need graphics: upload to Grafsy and come back to a finished video.
You need cuts, a second opinion and someone to catch a wrong number: use Claude and accept the longer time.
A client who must control every font and graphic: neither is the whole answer, so say that before you promise anything.
Whatever you use, watch the whole video before it goes out. A fast tool that never tells you the number is wrong just ships the mistake faster.

If you want to start a video service with this, I wrote a $4 guide called the Overlay Agency. It points to Grafsy, and I earn a share of the profit when someone buys Grafsy. I do not own Grafsy. Run the race yourself: one video, two ways, a clock and your own numbers.

Not precisely. Its page says it helps with fonts but does not guarantee them, so a client with strict brand fonts needs another route.
